channel.title: AI Daily Watch: VS Code, GitHub & developer tools
channel.description: Visual Studio Code, GitHub and GitHub Copilot, Visual Studio and Microsoft developer platforms.

item.title: GitHub Copilot usage metrics API adds code-review details and addressed rate
item.description: GitHub: GitHub added code-review feedback details to enterprise and organization Copilot usage metrics, including counts of comments evaluated and addressed and a per-repository addressed rate. The new breakdowns give administrators more information for assessing Copilot code-review outcomes.

item.title: GitHub Copilot usage metrics API flags telemetry and version gaps
item.description: GitHub: GitHub added per-user telemetry and version-compliance fields, plus aggregate counts, to Copilot usage metrics reports. The additions help administrators identify why usage reports may lack details and which users may need follow-up.

item.title: Microsoft presents Copilot upgrade agent for .NET Windows Arm64 migration
item.description: Microsoft: Microsoft described using the GitHub Copilot upgrade agent to assess and update .NET applications for Windows Arm64, including dependencies, platform assumptions, and project configuration. Developers can review proposed changes, but the post notes that a successful build is not a substitute for runtime testing on Windows Arm64.

item.title: GitHub secret scanning adds SpaceX partnership and upgrades detectors
item.description: GitHub: GitHub added SpaceX to its secret-scanning partnership program and introduced detection for a Starlink API secret. It also upgraded detectors for Alibaba, AWS, Google, OpenVSX, Pydantic Services, and Tencent with additional false-positive filtering, expanding coverage and refining alerts.

item.title: Microsoft shows how to run agentic coding locally with Foundry Local and GitHub Copilot
item.description: Microsoft: Microsoft described a local agentic-coding workflow that runs Qwen3.8-27B through Foundry Local and connects it to GitHub Copilot. The on-device approach is presented as offering more privacy, predictable inference costs, and continued work without a network connection.

item.title: CodeQL 2.27.4 improves query accuracy, metadata, and CLI security checks
item.description: GitHub: CodeQL 2.27.4 improves query accuracy across several languages, corrects query metadata, and adds security checks when bundling or publishing packs. The CLI also directs JVM warnings and initialization errors to standard error, preventing interference with machine-readable output.

item.title: GitHub Copilot plans to end support for JetBrains IDEs 2025.2.x
item.description: GitHub: Microsoft announced that the GitHub Copilot plugin will end support for JetBrains IDEs version 2025.2.x in the coming months, moving the minimum supported version to 2025.3.x. Existing installations are not expected to be immediately disabled, but users on affected versions may lose compatibility with future plugin updates and will no longer receive new features, fixes, or performance improvements for that IDE version.

item.title: Intelligent Terminal 0.3 adds agent-focused sidebar, session search, and headless mode
item.description: Microsoft: Intelligent Terminal 0.3 adds a sidebar for managing tabs and agent sessions, global search, agent filtering, and live status indicators. It can also keep selected tabs running in headless mode after the terminal window closes, and automatically detects supported agent CLIs for the new-tab menu.

item.title: GitHub Copilot becomes available in Xcode’s built-in coding assistant
item.description: GitHub: GitHub Copilot is now available in public preview within Xcode’s built-in coding assistant, starting with Xcode 27.3 beta. The separate GitHub Copilot for Xcode extension remains available, giving developers a native alternative rather than requiring migration.

item.title: Visual Studio Code 1.145 adds remote-agent previews, cron schedules, and chat controls
item.description: Microsoft: VS Code 1.145 adds the ability to preview apps and use canvases from remote agent sessions in the Agents window, along with cron-based automation schedules and chat-noise controls. The stable release was dated November 4, 2026.

item.title: WinApp VS Code extension v0.4 previews project-aware WinUI XAML IntelliSense
item.description: Microsoft: Microsoft released WinApp VS Code extension v0.4, adding an experimental preview of project-aware IntelliSense for WinUI XAML, a command to create WinUI apps, and the ability to build and run projects from VS Code. The extension is available in public preview, with full project-aware support for C# WinUI projects requiring the .NET 10 SDK.

item.title: Dependabot version updates add support for Agent Package Manager
item.description: GitHub: Dependabot now supports version updates for Agent Package Manager dependencies, opening pull requests for supported Git dependencies declared in apm.yml and regenerating apm.lock.yaml when present. The feature is generally available on github.com across plans; this update does not include security updates.

item.title: Copilot usage API separates BYOK and enterprise custom-model usage
item.description: GitHub: GitHub updated the Copilot usage metrics API to separately identify local BYOK activity and requests using enterprise custom models. The added reporting helps organizations review model usage and distinguish provider-billed or local-model use from Copilot-hosted usage; existing totals remain unchanged.

item.title: Dependabot adds support for Python 3.15
item.description: GitHub: Dependabot now supports Python 3.15, allowing projects using the new version to continue receiving updates. GitHub says support is available to all github.com users and will be included in GitHub Enterprise Server 3.24.

item.title: GitHub REST API adds a cost-center lookup for resources
item.description: GitHub: GitHub added a REST API endpoint to look up the cost center associated with a user, organization, repository, or enterprise team. The response returns the cost-center ID and name, simplifying billing and cost-center workflows that previously required scanning cost-center resource lists; access depends on the caller’s role.

item.title: GitHub Copilot becomes available in JetBrains Air
item.description: GitHub: GitHub Copilot is now available in JetBrains Air, where users can delegate coding tasks, work across parallel agent sessions, and review results in context. Cloud tasks can run through Air Teams using the user’s existing Copilot subscription rather than JetBrains AI credits.

item.title: CodeQL 2.27.3 adds Python 3.15 and JSON data-extension support
item.description: GitHub: CodeQL 2.27.3 adds support for Python 3.15 features, JSON syntax for data extensions, C23 bit-precise integers, and query-accuracy improvements. The update also changes the GitHub Actions control-flow graph implementation, which may require developers with custom queries to adjust them.

item.title: GitHub security risk assessments now show repository protection status
item.description: GitHub: GitHub’s code security and secret risk assessments now indicate whether findings are in protected or unprotected repositories, helping organizations spot where to extend security coverage. The improvement is available in GitHub Enterprise Cloud and GitHub Team; secret risk assessment support is slated for GitHub Enterprise Server 3.24.

item.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows weekly update highlights hardening and cost-aware routing
item.description: GitHub: GitHub’s November 2 Agentic Workflows roundup describes safer pull-request outputs, optional actions-lock integration, guided remediation, and additional workflows adopting model routing to keep lower-cost work economical. The post reports these project updates and notes that release v1.0.1 itself was published October 27.

item.title: Microsoft summarizes October Azure Developer CLI releases and features
item.description: Microsoft: Microsoft’s October Azure Developer CLI roundup covers releases 1.35.0 through 1.37.2. Highlights include deployment previews across multiple Azure services, Container Apps express deployments, a beta command for removing stored environment values, and support for extension-defined infrastructure providers in generated pipelines.

item.title: GitHub app in Microsoft Teams reaches general availability
item.description: Microsoft: The GitHub app in Microsoft Teams is now generally available, letting teams work with GitHub and Copilot in the context of their chats, channels, and meeting chats. Users can ask in natural language to select or switch repositories and choose which Copilot model to use for a task.

item.title: Visual Studio 2026 version 18.11.3 addresses security advisories
item.description: Microsoft: Microsoft released Visual Studio 2026 version 18.11.3 on October 29 with security advisory fixes. The listed issues include a libcurl HTTP/2 upload use-after-free, a Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write, and a Visual Studio certificate-validation vulnerability.

item.title: GitHub adds webhook delivery IP ranges to the Meta API
item.description: GitHub: GitHub added three webhook delivery IP ranges to the Meta API’s `hooks` field. Operators maintaining static allowlists should add the prefixes to avoid rejecting deliveries; the change applies across GitHub.com plans, including Enterprise Cloud.

item.title: Microsoft details vcpkg’s October update, including configurable cache compression
item.description: Microsoft: Microsoft summarized October changes to vcpkg, including a configurable binary-cache compression level, improved cache diagnostics and reliability, and updated ports such as Boost 1.92.0. The compression option lets developers trade ZIP archive size against cache submission time.

item.title: Microsoft and Syncfusion collaborate on open-source Blazor toolkit and contributions
item.description: Microsoft and Syncfusion: Microsoft announced a collaboration with Syncfusion to advance Blazor. Syncfusion has released a free, MIT-licensed component toolkit and contributed fixes and tests to ASP.NET Core and .NET scaffolding, adding reusable components while contributing directly to the platform.

item.title: Microsoft Copilot harness enters public preview in Foundry Agent Service
item.description: Microsoft: Microsoft introduced the Copilot harness in Foundry Agent Service as a public preview, giving developers a managed way to build agents that reason, use tools, and complete complex, long-running tasks. The post also announced general availability of long-running resilience for hosted agents.

item.title: Visual Studio Marketplace adds secretless Trusted Publishing for extensions
item.description: Microsoft: Microsoft announced Trusted Publishing for Visual Studio Marketplace extensions. GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines can use verified federated identity to publish without storing a long-lived personal access token or publishing secret; existing PAT-based publishing remains available.

item.title: Microsoft makes Copilot UX components generally available with SPFx 1.24
item.description: Microsoft: Microsoft made Copilot UX components generally available worldwide with SharePoint Framework 1.24, allowing developers to bring interactive dashboards, forms, and business actions into Copilot conversations. Components can also be reused in SharePoint, Teams, and Outlook; users need a Microsoft Copilot add-on license to render them in Copilot.

item.title: Copilot code review adds Max effort preview and generally available approvals
item.description: GitHub: GitHub added a Max effort level for Copilot code review in public preview and made Copilot approvals generally available. The combination is intended to provide a deeper review and an approval assessment within the pull-request review workflow.

item.title: Visual Studio Code 1.144 stable release expands agent workflows and continuity
item.description: Microsoft: VS Code 1.144 shipped in the stable channel with expanded agent workflows, including agent sessions that continue across environments and client continuity supported by the Agent Host Protocol. The release also brings agent management and model-selection updates, making it a substantial IDE update for developers using Copilot agents.

item.title: GitHub brings Copilot Agent Merge into cloud pull requests
item.description: GitHub: GitHub integrated Agent Merge into pull requests on GitHub.com. Copilot can watch for blockers such as failing Actions workflows and merge conflicts and attempt to fix them; the cloud feature is available to paid Copilot users subject to organization and enterprise policies.

item.title: GitHub Copilot Fusion reaches general availability for model routing
item.description: GitHub: Copilot Fusion is now generally available, letting users delegate model selection and orchestration to Copilot instead of choosing a model for each task. It is available across all Copilot plans in VS Code, the GitHub Copilot app, Copilot CLI, and JetBrains IDEs, with Standard, High, and Max effort levels.

item.title: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105 fixes Fusion effort selection in long-context sessions
item.description: GitHub: Copilot CLI 1.0.105 fixes an issue that prevented users from selecting Copilot Fusion High or Max from /model during long-context sessions. The official release page records publication on October 28.

item.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows reaches general availability
item.description: GitHub: GitHub Agentic Workflows is generally available on GitHub.com for Free, Team, and Enterprise. It lets users define reasoning-based automations in Markdown for compilation into GitHub Actions workflows, with GA additions including self-hosted runner support, improved budget forecasting, model routing, and stronger agent isolation.

item.title: Copilot Fusion previews intelligent routing between local and cloud models
item.description: GitHub: Copilot Fusion’s experimental preview can route requests between supported on-device and cloud models in Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, and VS Code. The announcement includes managed Windows setup for MAI Code 1.1 Flash and support for manually configured local models; it notes that routing still makes decisions in the cloud.

item.title: GitHub Copilot app adds Projects and computer use in public preview
item.description: GitHub: The GitHub Copilot app introduced Projects in public preview, providing a home for work spanning repositories and sessions. It also announced computer use in public preview on macOS and Windows, allowing Copilot to interact with desktop applications, including apps without APIs or MCP integrations.

item.title: GitHub Enterprise begins including access to Copilot for licensed users
item.description: GitHub: GitHub Enterprise customers working with a GitHub or Microsoft account team can now include Copilot access for each licensed user, with AI-credit budgeting applying to some capabilities. This changes how eligible enterprises manage Copilot access, while self-serve subscriptions remain unaffected and will receive availability in stages.

item.title: GitHub Copilot previews natural-language image generation and editing
item.description: GitHub: Copilot users can now generate and edit images with natural-language instructions without leaving Copilot. The feature is in public preview for Pro, Pro+, Business, and Enterprise plans, with image-token usage billed separately and counted against plan AI credits.

item.title: GitHub rolls out shared Copilot Automations for teams
item.description: GitHub: Shared Copilot Automations let teams build and maintain AI-powered workflows together in repositories. Automations are visible to repository readers, editable by those with write access, and billed to the repository owner; GitHub says rollout is underway for Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise plans.

item.title: GitHub introduces intelligence features for Copilot memory, context, and code search
item.description: GitHub: GitHub announced a context and learning layer for agents, including Copilot Memory, now generally available on paid plans, and Copilot dreaming, in public preview. Memory can carry personal preferences and repository conventions across sessions and clients, while dreaming reviews prior work to improve future agent sessions.

item.title: GitHub previews a Security extension for the Copilot app
item.description: GitHub: GitHub introduced a public-preview Security extension in the Copilot app that surfaces repository code-scanning alerts and lets users ask Copilot to explain or help fix them. The preview is available on github.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency; Enterprise Server is not supported.

item.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows introduces a pre-run admission gate
item.description: GitHub: GitHub Agentic Workflows now documents an opt-in admission gate that can consult a separately deployed authority before an agent session starts. The authority can approve or deny activation and return AI-credit allowances, enabling centralized policy and budgeting; the post emphasizes this is cooperative, not a hard quota.

item.title: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.104 changes Auto model selection and Autopilot task waiting
item.description: GitHub: Copilot CLI 1.0.104 changes managed fusion sessions to start on Auto and apply fusionTier settings. Interactive and SDK Autopilot sessions now continue waiting for attached background tasks instead of stopping at the configured timeout; `-p --autopilot` still honors that timeout.

item.title: VS Code adds configurable eagerness for GitHub Copilot inline suggestions
item.description: Microsoft: VS Code now lets paid GitHub Copilot subscribers choose low, medium, or high eagerness for inline suggestions. The settings let developers tune how proactively Copilot offers suggestions and how large its proposed edits are.

item.title: GitHub Copilot assisted permissions reach general availability
item.description: GitHub: GitHub made Copilot assisted permissions generally available in Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, and VS Code. The mode automatically proceeds with requests judged clearly safe and requires user approval for other requests; enterprise administrators can manage access to the mode.

item.title: GPT-6.1 Terra becomes generally available in GitHub Copilot
item.description: GitHub: GPT-6.1 Terra is now generally available in GitHub Copilot for Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise users, with rollout across VS Code, Visual Studio, CLI, the cloud agent, and other clients. GitHub positions it for everyday agentic coding and terminal work at a lower cost than GPT-6.1 Sol; usage-based billing follows provider list pricing.

item.title: Visual Studio adds resumable, unsaved Markdown investigation notes
item.description: Microsoft: Visual Studio 2026 version 18.11 can create standalone Markdown notes, and the opt-in Hot Exit preview can restore unsaved notes after Visual Studio is closed and reopened. This helps developers resume investigations without having to save the note or add it to a project first.

item.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows weekly update highlights hardening and safer credential handling
item.description: GitHub: GitHub Agentic Workflows’ October 26 weekly update recaps six hardening releases, emphasizing stronger static analysis, safer credential handling, and clearer diagnostics. Highlighted changes include network credentials for safe-output integration jobs and secret-safe error diagnostics for engine-driver crashes.
